_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Rename the building "canopy" to awning_like so it cannot be read as a tree canopy
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-27 (owner). "canopy" means the tree crown in ground, trees, lidar layers and canopy_grid/canopy_audit, and also a roof or cover over an entrance in feature specs. The owner's name for the building sense is awning_like (not only awnings: porch roofs, covered areas, canopies). Cause class: Translation (naming). Deliver: rename every building-sense use and leave tree uses alone. Known building-sense sites: facade_plan entrance field `canopy` and CANOPY_KINDS / _validate_canopy in lib/builds/facade_plan.py; the details kind 'canopy' in lib/builds/feature_build.py (detail kinds list and its handler) and the spec docstring there; rules/feature-builds.md; lib/builds/test_facade_plan.py and lib/builds/test_feature_build.py. Decide the name of the kind value 'canopy' inside the field (it is one kind of awning_like) and keep 'none', 'covered_area', 'awning'. Existing world specs that use the old key (worlds/southampton-build/site/builds/retail_w33830236.json) must be migrated, or the loader must refuse the old key with a message naming the new one; no silent alias. Leave lib/sources/test_lidar_query.py (tree layer) and ground/trees code alone. Proof: existing facade_plan and feature_build unit tests renamed and passing, plus a test that the old key is refused, plus a grep check that no tree module mentions awning_like. Helps: all feature builds; unblocks planning the SUSU entrance covered area without the ambiguity.

tasks.title: Footprint columns that no feature builds are left unowned, so neither ground nor the feature fills them
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-27 from the SUSU void review. Cause class: Capability (gap between two owners). ground_layer skips every column inside a mapped building footprint polygon (skipped 'building footprint'); feature_build can drop columns of its own footprint from the plan (footprint squaring, lidar-mass intersect, small-island drop), so a column can be inside the polygon yet in no plan. Nobody writes it, and a pit left in the baseline there survives every ground rerun and every feature rebuild. Observed: three columns in a mapped footprint, feature plan excludes them, baseline stone sits 8-11 blocks below lidar ground. Deliver, so it is resolvable whenever it recurs: (1) feature_build reports, in the dry run and in the plan summary, every column of its labelled footprints it left out of the plan, with the reason (squared off, lidar-mass, island); (2) ground_layer treats a footprint column as free ground when no built or planned feature owns it (use the cell journal / plan ownership, not live blocks), raising or lowering it to lidar ground height (lidar is the height truth); footprint columns that a feature does own stay untouched; (3) a check (cell_registry verify or reconcile, or an existing audit) lists footprint columns owned by no element so the gap is visible after the fact. Prefer extending existing reports over a new script. Proof: unit tests on MemoryBlocks: a footprint column excluded from a feature plan is surfaced by ground at lidar height; a column the feature owns is unchanged; the dry run lists dropped columns with reason. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, their tests, and rules/layered-passes or evidence-order wording if the footprint skip is documented there. Helps: every feature type that squares or intersects its footprint (halls, houses, terraces), every world. Place-specific cells go in the issue, not here.
